gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a power station used as the UPS for an existing sump pump has to be set up for that job. On the BLUETTI AC180, ECO mode switches the AC output off after 1, 2, 3 or 4 hours at or below a 15–30 W load, and a sump pump draws close to nothing between cycles. If ECO is left on, the first hours of an outage without inflow can leave the pump unpowered. Grid Enhancement also has to be off, or the advertised ≤20 ms switchover gets slower.
standout_why: Pages I read: the Consumer Reports buying guide, the CR 'Best Sump Pump Backup Systems' page, belowthesill.com/sump-pumps/backup and anvilfield.com's field guide. None of them covers portable power stations, UPS switchover, ECO auto-off or motor start surge. CR's guide says nothing about power stations or inverters. Belowthesill and Anvilfield mention no power station or UPS settings, and Anvilfield only says 'Lithium options exist'. ChatGPT's own answer lists 'Inverter + battery' at $400–$1,500+ with no setup caveat. Pages I did not open: ferguson.com, pumpendium.com, capablehome.com, callhome.help, angi.com, burlingtoncountyplumbers.com, secamerica.com, the ICLR booklets, SSPMA and a2gov. One of those could cover this, so the score is 2, not 3.
kit_items: Independent DC backup pump: Wayne ESP25 (Amazon lists it as ESP25n). It is a second 12 V pump with its own float, so it covers both a power cut and a failed primary pump. Wayne rates it at 1,680 GPH at 10 ft of lift and builds in an alarm that sounds while the DC pump runs.
Battery for the DC pump: Wayne WSB1275, a 75 Ah maintenance-free battery. Wayne's ESP25 page recommends it and says it is sold separately, so the ESP25 alone is not a working set.

Alternative, power for the existing AC pump: BLUETTI AC180 power station (1,152 Wh LiFePO4, 1,800 W rated, ≤20 ms UPS switchover). It only covers power loss, not a failed or stuck primary pump. For this job ECO must be off, Grid Enhancement must be off, and the pump's start surge has to fit within the AC180's limits. The manual warns that motors may start at 2–4× their rated power.
High-water alarm: ChatGPT and CR both recommend one. Not sourced or priced here.

Only solar bundles, none built for sump use: AC180 + SP100L $679.00, AC180 + 200 W solar $769.00, AC180 + 2×200 W $1,232.00, AC180 + 350 W $1,088.00 (350 W panel out of stock). The page says the AC180 is out of stock with restock expected late November, and also says 'ships from 12.14'.

findings.label: ECO mode auto-off
findings.value: AC output turns off after 1, 2, 3 or 4 h at a 15–30 W load (DC: 5–10 W)
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 - Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Manual: 'the AC/DC output will automatically turn off if the AC180 is bearing low or no load for a while.' It does not say whether ECO is on by default. Between cycles a float-switched sump pump draws close to nothing, so with ECO on the output can switch off before the next rise in water.

findings.label: UPS switchover time
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 - Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: The manual says to turn off Grid Enhancement for UPS use, because with it on 'the UPS takes longer to switch over'. It also says 'Test the function before use.' The UPS section lists '1440W Max.' without saying whether that is output or input.

findings.label: Motor start warning and surge
findings.value: 1,800 W rated; 2,700 W surge; motors may start at 2–4× rated power
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 - Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: The 2,700 W Power Lifting mode is for 'pure resistive loads' only (heaters, irons), is off by default, and does not help a pump motor. The manual says motor/compressor devices 'can easily overload the AC180'.

findings.value: $499.00; 1,152 Wh; LiFePO4, 3,500+ cycles; 1,800 W AC across 4 × 120 V outlets
